description: A binding proposal binds exact repository/commit/blob/path bytes, non-overlapping sorted byte spans with selected-byte digests, and a concrete object-shaped applicability selector.

A proposal with a bounded effective_until (unlike every other proposal fixture, which leaves it null) exercises the closed form of the effective interval and the intervals_overlap b_before_a_end term below.
Propositions supplied out of strict sort order are rejected rather than silently re-sorted.
Two source byte spans whose ranges overlap are rejected as ambiguous evidence coordinates.
A repository_version_id using the entity URI form instead of version is rejected: a version coordinate is not its parent entity's continuing identity.
A bounded proposal whose effective_until is at or before its own effective_from is rejected as invalid shape, independent of any two-binding overlap check.
The document author approves alongside an independent principal and the declared threshold is met; the receipt's separation-of-duty verdict is re-derived from the approvals, not merely trusted.

required_threshold is 1, so the lone author approval already meets the threshold; rejection comes only from the re-derived separation-of-duty verdict, which is false because no eligible approval comes from any principal other than the author, disagreeing with the fixture's falsely declared satisfied flag.

required_threshold is 1 and the lone author approval already meets it; separation_of_duty_satisfied is honestly declared false (agreeing with the re-derived verdict) and the receipt is still rejected, closing the (declared false, derived false) quadrant that receipt.author-only-approval.negative does not reach.
A single independent approval below the required threshold is rejected even though separation of duty alone would be satisfied.
An eligible-approvals list with a repeated principal or signer key is rejected.
A proposal's expected composite head (binding-family revision, registry package digest, activation-policy digest) goes stale when only the activation-policy digest changes.
An overlapping effective interval is accepted when the proposal explicitly names the active binding's statement as its supersession target.
The identical overlapping effective interval without an explicit supersession target is rejected as an incompatible overlap.

A bounded proposal whose effective_until ends before an active binding with an unbounded effective_from begins does not conflict, exercising intervals_overlap's b_before_a_end against the proposal's own upper bound rather than a hard-coded true.
The same bounded proposal against an active binding that starts inside its effective interval is a genuine overlap and is rejected absent an explicit supersession target.
Lifecycle events for activation and (separately) supersession bind the exact statement_id and the active registry_head under which the event was accepted.
A supersession-kind lifecycle event without an explicit supersedes_statement_id is rejected.
A supersession-kind lifecycle event naming its own statement_id as supersedes_statement_id is rejected; applying it would retire the very statement it names as its own successor.
Two independently accepted statement IDs for one binding family with unestablishable ordering are recorded as contested; dependent comparisons remain unknown.
A contested record naming only one distinct statement ID (even if duplicated) is rejected.
Normal activation policy rejects an effective time strictly before the accepted time.
A separately authorized, higher-threshold retroactive correction appends a new bitemporal interpretation naming a distinct prior as-known conclusion, which the correction never rewrites.
A correction whose effective time does not actually precede its accepted time is rejected; the hook is exclusive to genuinely retroactive corrections.

A genuinely retroactive correction naming the ordinary activation policy as its own authorizing_policy (same entry_id, same threshold as normal_activation_policy) is rejected: the exception must be authorized by a separately named policy declaring a strictly higher threshold, never by the policy it is exceptional relative to.
A supersession-kind lifecycle event with an explicit supersedes_statement_id binds its own statement_id and the active registry_head under which it was accepted.
